title: Licensing: Financial product advice and dealing
subject: This guide provides guidance on the meaning of 'provide financial product advice' and 'deal in a financial product' under the Corporations Act 2001. It also outlines the obligations that apply to providers of financial services, including licensing requirements and conduct standards.
background: The guide is issued under the Corporations Act 2001 and is intended for persons who provide financial product advice or deal in financial products, as well as their professional advisers such as lawyers. It aims to clarify the scope of the licensing regime and help entities understand when an Australian financial services (AFS) licence is required.
ruling: ASIC explains that providing financial product advice includes both personal advice and general advice, as defined in s 766B of the Corporations Act. Dealing in a financial product is defined in s 766C and includes activities such as applying for, acquiring, varying, or disposing of a financial product. ASIC states that a person must hold an AFS licence or be an authorised representative to provide such services, unless an exemption applies. The guide emphasises that advice and dealing activities are subject to the general obligations under s 912A, including the duty to act efficiently, honestly, and fairly. ASIC also clarifies that certain conduct, such as arranging a deal, may constitute dealing and trigger licensing requirements.
legislation_referenced: Australian Securities and Investments Commission Act 2001 (Cth) s 12DA
Australian Prudential Regulation Authority Act 1998 (Cth) s 3(2)
